countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.summary: First automatic UK test: 183 or more days in the UK in the tax year makes the person UK resident, unless an automatic overseas test is met first.
countries.legalReference: Finance Act 2013, Schedule 45; HMRC RDR3 section 3.1

otherTests.summary: First automatic overseas test: a person who was UK resident in at least one of the previous three tax years is automatically non-resident if they spend fewer than 16 days in the UK in the tax year.
Second automatic overseas test: a person who was not UK resident in any of the previous three tax years is automatically non-resident if they spend fewer than 46 days in the UK in the tax year.
Third automatic overseas test: full-time work abroad with fewer than 91 UK days and fewer than 31 UK workdays of over 3 hours makes the person automatically non-resident.
Second automatic UK test (only-home test): having your only home in the UK for 91+ consecutive days and staying there on at least 30 days in the tax year makes you resident.
Third automatic UK test: full-time work in the UK over a 365-day period makes the person resident; not a day-count rule.
Sufficient ties test, Table A (UK resident in 1+ of 3 prior years): the more UK days, the fewer UK ties needed to be resident; 5 ties are available, including the country tie.
Sufficient ties test, Table B (not UK resident in any of 3 prior years): 4 ties available; 46-90 days needs all 4, 91-120 needs 3, 121-182 needs 2.
Deeming rule: for someone previously UK resident with 3+ ties, days in the UK without a midnight stop being ignored after the first 30 and count as UK days.
Day-counting rule for all SRT tests: midnight presence counts, with exclusions for qualifying transit days and up to 60 exceptional-circumstances days per tax year.
